params.place: on the map: Egypt between two seas

moments.what: the canal draws itself through the desert, a cargo ship already in it
the camera follows the thin blue line
Egypt fills in, its name writes on
a red barrier swings shut across the water
a calendar tag drops onto the barrier

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What if the Suez Canal, one thin ditch in Egypt, closed for a whole year?

params.place: on the map: the world, every sea lane

moments.what: gold rings spread out from the canal
the camera pulls back to the whole world
shipping lanes light up across every ocean
the lanes through Suez glow brighter, ships slide along them
the camera closes on the canal, its share on a tag
boxes of phones stack on a passing ship
a car carrier slides in
a tanker follows

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In 2021, about 12% of the world's trade sailed through this one strip of water: phones, clothes, cars and oil.

params.place: on the old map: the isthmus of Suez

moments.what: small diggers cut a line through the sand
the sand heaps up either side
water floods in, the year writes on
the camera pulls out over Africa
a long dashed route round Africa is crossed out

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It was dug through the desert and opened in 1869, so ships could skip the long way round Africa.

params.place: on the map: China to Europe

moments.what: a container ship leaves Shanghai
a pin drops on Rotterdam
the route draws across the Indian Ocean
the camera follows it up the Red Sea
it slips through the canal into the Mediterranean

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So a ship from China reaches Europe the short way: across the Indian Ocean, up the Red Sea and through the canal, into the Mediterranean.

params.place: on the map: the canal, close

moments.what: the camera dives to the canal
a huge container ship sails in
its name writes on its hull
the ship swings and jams
it locks across the banks, the water stops
its stern digs into the far bank, sand flies

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So what happens when it is blocked? In 2021, one giant ship, the Ever Given, got stuck sideways across it, its nose in one bank and its tail in the other.

params.place: on the map: both ends of the canal

moments.what: a DAY counter starts ticking
the counter climbs to the figure
ships arrive at the north end
and at the south end, lining up
the camera pulls back on two long queues
the view lifts higher, the queues still in sight

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: For 6 days, nothing moved, and ships piled up at both ends, in a queue you could see from space.

params.place: on the map: Africa and the Cape

moments.what: the barrier slams down on the canal
a lock icon stamps on it
a calendar flips through the months
the ships stop and spin, question marks over them
the ships turn back south
a new route draws all the way round Africa
a pin drops on the Cape of Good Hope

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now close it for a year. Where does every ship go? It turns around and takes the long way, past the tip of Africa.

params.place: on the map: two routes, two ships

moments.what: two ships set off from Asia side by side
one takes the canal route, one the Cape route
the Cape ship falls behind
an extra-days counter climbs on the slow ship
more ships follow it round
a fuel gauge on the slow ship drops

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Race the two routes, and the long way costs about 10 more days at sea on a trip from Asia to Europe, and a lot more fuel.

params.place: on the map: the world from above

moments.what: the camera rises over the world
stacks of containers pile up at both ends of the canal
the figure lands on the stack
the camera closes on the canal again
the queue lines stretch on and on

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Remember, that one blockage held up about $9.6B of goods every day. Close it for a year, and that jam would never, ever end.

params.place: on the map: the two canals, then Egypt again

moments.what: a pin glows on Suez
a pin glows on Panama
a question mark bounces between them
a comment bubble pops up beside the pins
the camera dives back to Egypt: the first frame

beats.say: Suez or Panama: which shortcut would hurt the world more? Tell me down below in the comments. Now picture it one more time:
